measured_by: Direct gh api queries against Expensify/App plus primary-source reads of contributingGuides/ and .github/
note: Every figure here is reproducible with the queries in queries.md. Re-measure before trusting anything older than a quarter; Expensify changes this process often (MelvinBot and ProposalPolice are both recent).

funnel.implication: About 4 genuinely new bounty opportunities per week. This is a small funnel, not a firehose.

melvinbot.presence_rate: 20 of 20 open Help Wanted issues sampled
melvinbot.implication: MelvinBot posting is the earliest reliable signal that an issue has entered the bounty pipeline. Treat it as the starting gun.

work_window.definition: Time from issue creation to the Help Wanted label being applied. Proposals are only accepted after the label.
work_window.implication: Median about two days of preparation time, but the floor is four hours. Never assume you have days.

competition.implication: Multiple contributors run automation that fires a pre-written multi-kilobyte proposal within one to two seconds of the label. Nobody writes 7KB in two seconds; the analysis happens during the work window.

98426.selected_by: Ollyws (C+) on 2026-08-21 with the comment: 'I think we can just drop the redundant !!rate check here so @abbasifaizan70's proposal LGTM. woo C+ reviewed'
98426.why_it_won: Permalink-cited causal chain across four files (RateField.tsx -> MenuItem.tsx -> useDistanceRequestState.ts -> DistanceRequestUtils.ts), each pinned to a full commit SHA with a line range.
98426.notable_loser: neerajbachani posted a 19370-byte proposal six hours later and lost. Length did not beat timing plus precision.

98791.note: Fourteen proposals landed inside sixty seconds. Three days later the assigned C+ (linhvovan29546) was still commenting 'Can anyone reproduce the crash?'. A contributor who supplied real reproduction steps became the most useful participant on the thread.
98791.implication: Reproduction is the scarce good on hard issues, not another fast proposal.

proposal_police.mechanism: An OpenAI conversation per issue holds every proposal posted so far. A new proposal scoring at or above 90 percent similarity to a still-live proposal is automatically edited into a withdrawal.
also_does: classifies comments that do not follow the proposal template
grades edits made to existing proposals
exempt: Expensify employees (checked via org team membership)
proposal_police.observed_effect: On issue 98791, four of the first wave of sniped proposals were auto-withdrawn as duplicates.

selection_rule.source: contributingGuides/PROPOSAL_TEMPLATE.md, inside an HTML comment addressed to Contributor+ reviewers
selection_rule.quote: Choose the first proposal that has a reasonable answer to all the required questions.
selection_rule.supporting_quote: Do not approve any proposals that lack a satisfying explanation to the first two prompts. It is CRITICALLY important that we understand the root cause at a minimum even if the solution doesn't directly address it.
selection_rule.implication: Root cause outranks solution. The bar is 'reasonable and complete', not 'best'. Being complete beats being clever, and being early beats being thorough-but-late.

payment.timing: No less than 7 days after the PR is deployed to production, to allow for regression testing
payment.regression_penalty: 50 percent penalty to both Contributor and C+ per regression, within a 168-hour regression window after production deploy
payment.new_contributor_limit: One job at a time. Do not submit proposals for new jobs until your first PR has been merged.
